title: U.S. Senate · New Hampshire

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Sen. Jeanne Shaheen (D) is retiring and did not run in the September 8, 2026 Democratic primary. U.S. Rep. Chris Pappas won that primary with 64.6% of the vote over Karishma Manzur and others. John Sununu (a businessman and former faculty member, not to be confused with his father, former Gov. John H. Sununu, or his brother, Gov. Chris Sununu) won the Republican primary with 68.4% over Scott Brown. Sununu previously served one term in the U.S. Senate (2003-2009) after defeating Shaheen in 2002; Shaheen defeated him in a 2008 rematch. He announced his candidacy on October 22, 2025 after Shaheen announced her retirement.

candidates.name: Chris Pappas
candidates.ballotNote: Won the September 8, 2026 Democratic primary with 64.6% of the vote.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for New Hampshire's 1st District (since 2019)

summary.text: Chris Pappas is the Democratic nominee for the open New Hampshire U.S. Senate seat. A Manchester native who co-owns his family's restaurant, he served in the state House, as Hillsborough County treasurer and on the Executive Council before winning New Hampshire's 1st District U.S. House seat in 2018. He announced his Senate campaign in April 2025 after Sen. Jeanne Shaheen said she would not seek re-election.

background.text: Born in Manchester, New Hampshire, in 1980; graduated from Manchester Central High School in 1998. His great-grandfather founded what is now the family-owned Puritan Backroom restaurant in Manchester.
Earned a bachelor's degree in government from Harvard in 2002.
Is a co-owner of his family's restaurant, the Puritan Backroom; his House website describes him as a lifelong Manchester resident and small business owner.
Volunteered on Jeanne Shaheen's 1996 gubernatorial campaign as a high school student. Elected to the New Hampshire House of Representatives in 2002 and served two terms.

Served as treasurer of Hillsborough County from 2007 to 2011 (he lost a 2010 re-election bid to Bob Burns), then won the Executive Council seat for District 4 in 2012 by defeating Burns, serving until 2019.

Won the Democratic primary for New Hampshire's 1st Congressional District in 2018 and has represented the district in the U.S. House since; he was the first openly gay U.S. House member elected from New Hampshire.
In the House he serves on the Transportation and Infrastructure and Veterans' Affairs committees, and is co-chair of the Congressional Equality Caucus.
Announced his Senate candidacy on April 3, 2025, and won the September 8, 2026 Democratic primary with 64.6% of the vote over Karishma Manzur (33.2%).

priorities.text: Says he is focused on affordability and the economy, working to lower costs for families and small businesses on utilities, groceries, child care, health care and housing.
His campaign says he called for a ban on stock trading by members of Congress and forced a floor vote on the issue, and worked to cap the cost of insulin at $35.

positions.summary: On the New Hampshire Executive Council, voted to expand Medicaid to bring down health care costs and increase access for tens of thousands of Granite Staters.
His campaign says he authored the Small Business RELIEF Act, which would exempt New Hampshire small businesses from global baseline and reciprocal tariffs and refund tariffs already paid.
positions.quote: His Small Business RELIEF Act would exempt New Hampshire small businesses from global baseline and reciprocal tariffs

positions.summary: His campaign site says he is fighting to restore and codify the rights established under Roe, and that he helped pass the Women's Health Protection Act in the House.
positions.quote: Chris is fighting to restore and codify the rights established under Roe and safeguard access to reproductive health care.

positions.summary: His campaign site says ICE should focus on deporting people who are here illegally and are violent, that he helped block an ICE detention facility in Merrimack, and that he supported legislation to fund 22,000 border patrol agents.
positions.quote: Chris believes that ICE must focus on their core mission: ensuring that individuals who are here illegally, who are violent, and breaking our laws are deported.

record.text: Sits on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs and the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: John Sununu
candidates.ballotNote: Won the September 8, 2026 Republican primary with 68.4% of the vote over Scott Brown.
candidates.currentRole: Former U.S. Senator (2003-2009); faculty member, St. Anselm College

summary.text: John Sununu is the Republican nominee for the open New Hampshire U.S. Senate seat. A mechanical engineer and MBA who worked in engineering, consulting and manufacturing, he served in the U.S. House from 1997 to 2003 and in the Senate from 2003 to 2009, losing his 2008 re-election bid to Jeanne Shaheen. He announced this campaign in late 2025 for the seat Shaheen is vacating.

background.text: Born in Boston, Massachusetts, on September 10, 1964, one of eight siblings; son of former New Hampshire Gov. John H. Sununu (R) and brother of former Gov. Chris Sununu (R).
Earned bachelor's and master's degrees in mechanical engineering from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (1986 and 1987) and an MBA from Harvard (1991).
Career experience before Congress included engineering, consulting and manufacturing work and running operations at an electronics company.
Won the open 1st District U.S. House seat in 1996 by defeating Democrat Joe Keefe, and was re-elected in 1998 and 2000; he served on the House Appropriations and Budget committees.
Elected to the U.S. Senate in 2002 after defeating incumbent Sen. Bob Smith in the Republican primary and Gov. Jeanne Shaheen in the general election; Shaheen defeated him in a 2008 rematch.

After leaving the Senate, served as a faculty member at St. Anselm College and as a director at Boston Scientific, joined the law firm Akin Gump as an adjunct senior policy advisor in 2010, and was named to Lloyd's of London's governing council in 2019.
Announced his 2026 campaign in late 2025, received President Trump's endorsement, and won the September 8, 2026 Republican primary with 68.4% of the vote over Scott Brown (26.4%).

priorities.text: In an interview with The Dartmouth, said New Hampshire needs "an effective voice in Washington" focused on "the economy, jobs, affordability, housing, energy and healthcare," and described Congress as dysfunctional.
priorities.quote: Politics isn't just about holding an office. It's about being an effective voice for the people you represent. Right now, New Hampshire needs someone who understands the state and who is focused on the right things: the economy, jobs, affordability, housing, energy and healthcare.

positions.summary: In a May 2026 interview with The Dartmouth he said the War Powers Act is appropriately structured because it lets the administration respond to imminent threats while preserving Congress' authority afterward, and that U.S. actions involving Iran have been consistent with precedent.
positions.quote: I think the War Powers Act is appropriately structured because it allows the administration to respond to imminent threats while preserving Congress’ authority afterward.

record.text: As a U.S. Senator (2003-2009), served on Senate committees during the 108th-110th Congresses; specific committee assignments and roll-call votes from that earlier tenure were not reviewed for this entry.

candidates.researchNotes: Sununu has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; priorities drawn from a media interview quoted by Ballotpedia.

candidates.name: Edmond Laplante

summary.text: Edmond Laplante is the Constitution Party nominee for the open New Hampshire U.S. Senate seat. He is a Marine Corps veteran and longtime automotive mechanic who, in his Ballotpedia survey response, lists himself as New Hampshire state chairman of the Constitution Party and a member of the SAU93 (Richmond) school board.

background.text: Born in Gardner, Massachusetts; earned a high school diploma from Montachusett Regional Vocational Tech and graduated from the Ohio Diesel and Gas Technical Institute in 1988.
Served in the U.S. Marine Corps from 1999 to 2007.
In his 2026 Ballotpedia survey response, describes himself as an auto mechanic for more than 40 years, with a "master tech degree," an associate degree in aviation science and an A&P license.

Is New Hampshire state chairman of the Constitution Party and a member of the SAU93 (Richmond) school board, according to his survey response; Ballotpedia notes a past affiliation with the Richmond Swanzey Republican Town Committee.

priorities.text: In his Candidate Connection survey, lists his three key campaign messages as constitutional compliance and limited government, protecting people's liberty, rights and financial well-being, and transparency and accountability.
Ending U.S. involvement in wars abroad and returning power to the states, per his campaign platform page.

statements.quote: immigration policy must begin with enforcement of the laws already on the books, and that individuals who are in the country illegally should not receive state or federal benefits intended for citizens and lawful residents.
statements.context: On his campaign website platform page

statements.quote: For civilian healthcare, including mental health and addiction treatment, solutions should be led by the states and communities closest to the people affected, not imposed by distant federal bureaucracies.
statements.context: On his campaign website platform page
